messages:
oncall-bot: Paging: multiple 429s observed fetching model artifacts from hf.co during cold starts across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Initial spike at 09:42 UTC. Severity: P2. @vikram assigned :rotating_light:

vikram: seeing it in the runtime metrics dashboard too. Cold starts failing with model pull errors, cache miss rate up 12%.

sara: confirmed from logs — hf GETs returning 429 / rate-limited. sample: 
```
2026-02-18T09:42:12Z ERROR model-fetcher fetch failed: GET https://huggingface.co/models/rwkv/quantized/resolve/main/model.safetensors -> 429 Too Many Requests
stack: fetchArtifact -> openStream -> writeCache
```

eli: We have two main customer-impact paths: (1) new cold starts that attempt to fetch and time out, (2) pre-warm jobs hitting hf for many models. Current error rate ~18% of model pulls.

carlos: is this only hf.co or also S3-backed registries?

sara: only HF hub calls. S3 mirrors unaffected.

vikram: quick mitigation options: (A) enable local artifact mirror for pinned models (we already run a mirror for top-tier customers, can expand), (B) increase exponential backoff + jitter, (C) temporarily serve smaller quantized variant from our cache if available. We should also throttle pre-warm concurrency.

julia: I'll take on pre-warm throttle change. Where is that config?

eli: runtime/autoscaler -> prewarm.concurrencyLimit. set from 500 -> 50 for 15m. I'm pushing a short-lived k8s configmap change.

ops-runner: pushing patch to throttle pre-warm now. kubectl apply -f prewarm-throttle.yaml
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  prewarm.concurrencyLimit: "50"
```

ops-runner: applied at 09:55 UTC.

oncall-bot: Note: deploy-bot reports canary rollout 1/3 success for the throttling change.

vikram: Sara, can you trigger selective mirror fallback for the biggest 10 models? Script below.

sara: running script to flip mirror flag for pinned models: 
```
for m in $(cat top10.txt); do curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/models/$m/fallback" -d '{"use_local_mirror":true}'; done
```

sara: done at 10:01 UTC. initial checks: model pull error rate dropped from 18% -> 7% for mirrored models.

eli: good. For non-mirrored models, still seeing 429s. I'll deploy a prioritized prefetch of the 50 hottest models into the mirror. This will take ~12m.

carlos: customer impact note: ticket intake shows 3 customers with degraded responses for chat endpoints between 09:42-10:10 UTC. No large-scale user-facing outages reported yet.

oncall-bot: Incident status updated to: partial degradation; customers affected: subset of cohorts; action items assigned.

vikram: Also reached out to Hugging Face status via support channel and opened an incident with HF support (case #HF-8273).

hf-status-bot: HF status page: https://status.huggingface.co/ - reporting intermittent rate limiting due to high global pull volume. (link)

eli: mitigation so far: throttle pre-warm, enable mirror fallback for pinned models, prioritized prefetch. Next: add temporary client-side exponential backoff (3 retries -> 6 with base 500ms) for fetcher and increase model fetch concurrency limit per host to avoid stampeding on backoff.

vikram: I'll push a small runtime patch to increase retry/retry-after handling and to honor Retry-After headers from HF. Patch prepping now.

ops-runner: rolling patch to model-fetcher service (canary first). Deploying at 10:20 UTC.

sara: after canary, observed fewer immediate 429s and smoother backoff. Cold starts still slow but completing.

julia: I'm taking over oncall at 10:30 UTC. handing off: primary mitigations in place, HF still rate-limiting but impact reduced. Please ping if it spikes again.

vikram: notes for follow-up: (1) permanent artifact mirror strategy evaluation, (2) better pre-warm isolation from external registries, (3) add HF rate-limit metrics to alerts.

eli: created a runbook ticket: RB-195 add mirror expansion + alerting.

carlos: customer comms draft: "We experienced elevated model pull failures between 09:42-10:30 UTC due to rate limiting from a third-party model host (Hugging Face). We implemented throttling and mirror fallbacks; most affected traffic recovered by 10:10 UTC and full mitigation by 10:35 UTC. If you saw degraded responses, please contact support." Will post after legal review.

oncall-bot: Severity downgraded to P3 at 10:40 UTC.

vikram: final note: HF confirmed they were throttling large anonymous pulls and pushing a global mitigation; they advise clients to use mirrors/tokens. HF support suggests authenticating requests to increase quota.

sara: follow-up tasks added to the incident board. Will draft a short postmortem (lessons: mirror-first for pinned models, pre-warm concurrency safeguards, honor Retry-After headers).

julia: tagging @product & @support for customer impact tracking.

oncall-bot: Incident thread closed to new replies at 11:05 UTC. Postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1812345678/postmortem
